newsitem.title: GERMANY: German M3 growth slows, as expected, in March.
newsitem.headline: German M3 growth slows, as expected, in March.

text.p: German M3 money supply growth slowed down to an annualised, seasonally-adjusted rate of 8.3 percent in March against the average of the final quarter of 1996 compared with growth of 9.1 percent in February, the Bundesbank said on Monday.
M3 growth in March was fuelled by strong lending to the public sector and by a weakening of money capital formation, the Bundesbank said in a statement.
But strong outflows of funds in foreign transactions and a slowdown in bank lending to the private sector acted as brakes on M3 growth in March, the Bundesbank said.
The figure was in line with economists' expectations for growth of about 8.5 percent.

Adolf Rosenstock, economist at Industrial Bank of Japan, said in an initial reaction to the data, "The headline 8.3 percent is just what markets expected. The details are rather confusing. Lending to the private sector slowed down more than expected. and monetary capital formation was also weak. We were right for the wrong reasons".
German bonds barely reacted to the figures, the market still down in line with a sharp fall in French bonds on expectations that French elections will be called soon.
The June Bund future was at 100.68, down from 100.82 at Friday's close.
German shares also remained lower, unmoved after the March M3 data came in as expected.
The market had already been pressured by weak Bunds and the slide in the dollar against the mark and continued to be held back by expectations of a further U.S. rate rise in May.
The IBIS-DAX index measuring electronic trade was down 38.27 points at 3,322.93.
